correctness.rationale: Orthogonal monomials give K(t)=1+t/a+t²/[ab(1-t)]=(1-At-Bt²)/(1-t). The reciprocal series has c1=1/a, c2=(a-b)/(a²b), and c_n=A c_(n-1)+B c_(n-2) from n=3. Complete Pick requires nonvanishing (a kernel zero between two disc points would make the scalar values 1 and 0 pass the two-point Pick test, impossible for a contractive analytic multiplier by the maximum principle). Thus negative Taylor coefficients rule it out. The c2 and c3 tests exclude b>a and a<1, and leave only b=1 when a=1. If 1≤b≤a, the recurrence is nonnegative and both root moduli are below one: the positive root is below one by 1-A-B=1/(ab)>0 and dominates the other in modulus. If a>1 and b<1, the discriminant is [b(a+1)²-4a]/(a²b). When it is nonnegative, both roots are between zero and A<1, and c2/c1=A+a(-B)>A ensures nonnegative coefficients by the divided difference of the root powers, with a nonnegative derivative in the double-root case. In both cases the series is analytic on the disc and |F(t)|≤F(|t|)=1-1/K(|t|)<1, giving the normalized complete Pick criterion. Below the threshold, the roots q exp(±i theta) give coefficients proportional to sin((n-1)theta+phi), with positive amplitude and phi,theta in (0,pi/2). Crossing pi strictly gives the stated floor index even when a coefficient vanishes at phase pi, since the next phase is below 3pi/2. Using sin(theta)=sqrt(-Delta)/(2q), q→(a-1)/(2a), and phi=O(theta) from the phase numerator's positive limit gives the claimed scaled delay constant. The line defining u and the subsequent reference to nu are a local notation typo: the displayed expression is the unique sine weight fixed by c1 and c2, used consistently in this check. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; finite coefficient tests cannot replace the proof.
